name: Hip adduction
pattern: Legs pull in toward the midline against resistance, seated, lying, standing or squeezing a ball.
setup: Seated machine: back on the pad, knees and hips about 90°, pads on the inside of your knees.
Start with the legs only as wide as feels comfortable in the groin.
Hold the handles and sit tall.

steps.text: Legs apart, a light stretch on the inner thighs.
Squeeze for a moment with the pads together.
Let the legs open slowly to the start.

cues.cue: Open only as wide as you control.
cues.why: The groin is most often strained at long lengths; build range over weeks.

cues.cue: Sit tall and keep your hips on the seat.
cues.why: Leaning or lifting the hips turns the pull into a body throw.
Slow lengthening is the part that builds groin resilience.

cues.cue: Band, side-lying and ball-squeeze versions all work the adductors hard.
cues.why: Several simple adduction exercises reach high adductor longus activity.

breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze in, in as the legs open.

tempo.note: Squeeze in 1 second, hold 1, open in 2.

mistakes.name: Starting too wide
mistakes.looks: The legs are forced into a deep straddle at the start.
mistakes.fix: Set the machine narrower and widen it over time.
mistakes.why: A sudden heavy stretch is how adductor strains happen.

mistakes.name: Slamming the pads
mistakes.looks: The legs snap shut and the weight crashes back.
mistakes.fix: Pause when the pads meet and open slowly.
mistakes.why: Momentum skips the slow lengthening half.

mistakes.name: Hips lift or trunk leans
mistakes.looks: The hips come off the seat or the body rocks forward to help.
mistakes.fix: Sit tall against the pad and lighten the load.
mistakes.why: The hip flexors and body swing take over from the adductors.

safety: Groin pain: start with a ball squeeze at a pain-free effort and build up.
Never force the start position wider than you can control.

variants.change: Standing with a cable or band at the ankle: sweep the leg in across the standing leg.
Side-lying: lift the bottom leg 15-20 cm with the top leg crossed in front.
Squeeze a ball between the knees and hold 5-10 seconds.
Adduction pressure added to a bridge or split squat: hold the pad between the knees.

subtypes.name: Side-lying adduction
subtypes.change: Lie on your side, top leg crossed in front with the foot down; lift the straight bottom leg. Lift about 15-20 cm.

subtypes.name: Standing cable or band adduction
subtypes.change: Stand side-on to the anchor and pull the near leg in past the standing leg.

subtypes.name: Ball squeeze
subtypes.change: Lying on your back, knees bent, squeeze a ball between the knees and hold. Tracking: hold.

motion.basis: Default is the seated adduction machine. Start width estimated (machines allow about 30-50° per side); adductor exercise choice from serner2014; slow eccentric and range progression from haroy2019.

sources.cite: Serner A, Jakobsen MD, Andersen LL, Hölmich P, Sundstrup E, Thorborg K. EMG evaluation of hip adduction exercises for soccer players: implications for exercise selection in prevention and treatment of groin injuries. Br J Sports Med. 2014;48(14):1108-1114.
Harøy J et al. The Adductor Strengthening Programme prevents groin problems among male football players: a cluster-randomised controlled trial. Br J Sports Med. 2019;53(3):150-157.
Hölmich P et al. Effectiveness of active physical training as treatment for long-standing adductor-related groin pain in athletes: randomised trial. Lancet. 1999;353(9151):439-443.
